rules: This is a plate-heavy paper: eighteen numbered figures covering thirty-six measured panels and eight numbered grids covering eight regions, forty-four regions in all with nothing left over. Fourteen of the eighteen figures are multi-panel - two panels on Figures 1, 4, 5, 11, 12 and 13, three on Figures 9, 10, 14, 15, 17 and 18 - and every one is recorded as composite-panel with its later panels excluded as fragment-of-other rather than counted again [geometry.family] [geometry.panel_count] [geometry.panel_layout] [place.doc_order].

No plate prints a shared axis: every panel in every plate is drawn inside its own frame with its own ticks, and even the pairs whose y or x ranges coincide to the digit (Figures 11, 12 and 13 on 0-200000, Figures 17 and 18 on 2017-2021) are separate axes. shared_axes is therefore false on all eighteen rows [geometry.shared_axes].

Family tracks the section, not the plate count: the four schematics of the model and strategy sections and the memo's clip-art chain are flowchart-or-schematic, the three ACF/PACF and price plates of 3.2.1 are composite-panel, the robustness and yield plates of 4.2 and 5.2 are composite-panel, and the single quantitative plate of 3.4.1 is a line. There is no bar chart, no scatter, no map and no surface anywhere in the paper: nothing is drawn in three dimensions and nothing prints a colour bar [geometry.family] [geometry.three_d] [geometry.colorbar] [place.section_kind].

Caption side is decided per exhibit type and holds without exception: all eighteen figure captions are printed below their artwork except Figure 16, whose caption is the first line of the p21 memorandum page and therefore sits above its three ellipses, and all eight table captions are printed above their grid [caption.position].

Both caption vocabularies are the colon form - 'Figure N: ...' and 'Table N: ...' on every one of the twenty-six rows - and no caption carries a unit, a condition or a conclusion. Only Figures 11, 12 and 13 name a variable in the caption ('The impact of wL / wH / m on total assets'), and they name it once each [caption.numbering] [caption.voice] [caption.units] [caption.variables] [caption.concludes].

The paper cites its plates with a lowercase ligature verb in seven places: 'shown in the ﬁgure 5', 'shown in the ﬁgure 6', 'shown in the ﬁgure 7', 'shown in the ﬁgure below', 'The ﬁgure 9 shows', 'shown in the ﬁgure 10' and 'the ﬁgure 11, ﬁgure 12, ﬁgure 13'. That makes as-shown-in the dominant lead pattern, with figure-n-shows on Figures 4, 9 and 14 and direct on Tables 1, 3, 6, 7 [mention.lead_pattern] [mention.style] [mention.count].

Six rows are never called by number: Figure 2, Figure 3, Figure 16, Figures 17 and 18 and Table 8. Three of those - the memo plate, the two appendix plates - are in the back matter and are never discussed at all; Figure 2 and Figure 3 are named only by their captions; and Table 8 is introduced as 'the table below'. Their first_page is null rather than borrowed from the caption line [mention.first_page] [mention.lead_pages].

Where a number is printed the citation lands on the plate's own page on seventeen rows and exactly one page before it on three: Figure 4 (named on p7, printed on p8), Figure 13 (named in the p16 sentence that announces Figures 11, 12 and 13 together) and Figure 15 (named on p18, printed on p19). No row is cited more than one page early and no row is cited after its plate [mention.lead_pages].

Only the first two grids use bare booktabs; the six numeric grids - Tables 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8 - each add one vertical rule after the stub column, which is the paper's only departure from rules-only typesetting. No grid uses zebra striping, a merged cell, a diagonal header, a unit in the header or a continuation marker; Tables 3 and 6 carry a NOTE row and Tables 5, 7 and 8 are set landscape because the three strategy columns do not fit the text measure [table.rule_style] [table.zebra] [table.merged_cells] [table.diagonal_header] [table.units_in_header] [table.continued] [table.note_sentence] [table.orientation].

Table shape follows data size in a straight line: two-body-row grids for a paired p-value test and a two-cost sensitivity, three for a method lookup, four for the memorandum digest, six for the parameter list and the strategy results, seven for the parameter adjustment and eleven for the notation list. Numeric alignment is claimed only where the columns are numeric and the crop shows aligned decimal points: four grids carry it and Table 8's centred figures do not [table.rows] [table.cols] [table.numeric_cols] [table.decimal_aligned] [table.width].

Reading sentences are attached to the plates that carry a claim: Figures 4, 9, 13, 14 and 15 and Tables 2, 6, 7 and 8 are read out loud, while the four schematics, the appendix plates and the parameter grids are never interpreted. Where a plate is read, the reading is formulaic - 'It can be seen from the figure that ...', 'It can be seen that ...', 'Through the data in the table, we can find that:' - and the interpretation, not the plot, carries the conclusion [mention.trail_sentence] [mention.read_sentences].
